profile_anchor.decision: optimize the four-row Q4_K target-verification kernel before draft proposal fusion

hypothesis: For exactly four target-verification rows, extending the proven weight-decode-shared AVX2 Q4_K multi-accumulator kernel will outperform llama.cpp's current four-row tail GEMM by avoiding its Q4/Q8 lane-rearrangement network while retaining one Q4 decode per weight tile.

implementation.control: Pinned llama.cpp plus cache-order ragged dispatch v1 and fused one-to-three-row AVX2 v2
implementation.candidate: The identical source plus a v3 patch that extends the fused kernel to four accumulators and dispatches exactly four Q8_K rows through it

stop_rules: Reject on any control-versus-candidate exact-greedy token mismatch.
Reject if the paired four-row real-model graph improves by less than ten percent.
Reject if four-prompt MTP3 accepted throughput improves by less than five percent.
Reject if target-only accepted throughput regresses by more than two percent.
Do not run CUTE when a correctness or throughput gate has already rejected the candidate.
Preserve a terminal negative receipt instead of tuning thresholds after observing results.
claim_boundary: A pass promotes one AVX2 Q4_K four-row verification kernel on four Milan cores. It is not evidence for a trained approximation, final-node scaling, broad capability preservation, 100 accepted tokens per second, or scientific novelty.
